findings.title: isTeamAdminOrOwner requires admin AND owner (&&) instead of OR
findings.body: The check `const isTeamAdminOrOwner = (await isTeamAdmin(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0)) && (await isTeamOwner(user.id, booking.eventType?.teamId ?? 0));` uses `&&`, so it is only true when the user is simultaneously a team admin AND a team owner. In Cal.com's membership model a user has a single role, so this expression is effectively always false. As a result, legitimate team admins and team owners of team event types are always denied with FORBIDDEN when trying to add guests — the feature is completely broken for team bookings. This should be `||`.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the requester's credentials instead of the organizer's
findings.body: The handler builds `new EventManager({ ...user, credentials: [...credentials] })` from `getUsersCredentials(ctx.user)` — i.e. the credentials of whoever called the endpoint — even though the booking's organizer (with credentials) was already loaded via `booking.user.credentials`. When anyone other than the organizer adds guests (a team admin or an attendee, both of which the permission check explicitly allows), `eventManager.updateCalendarAttendees(evt, booking)` attempts to update the organizer's calendar event using credentials that have no access to it. Worse, this call is outside any try/catch and runs after the DB update, so the attendees are already persisted but the mutation throws and the calendar event is never updated — attendees get no calendar invite on the real event and the client shows an error despite the guests having been added.

findings.title: No validation of booking status or time — guests can be added to cancelled/rejected/past bookings
findings.body: After fetching the booking, the handler never checks `booking.status` or whether the booking has already ended. Guests can therefore be added to CANCELLED or REJECTED bookings (receiving CONFIRMED ics invites and scheduled emails for an event that does not exist) and to bookings in the past. The UI partially hides this (the edit menu is rendered for past confirmed bookings too, via the `isBookingInPast && isConfirmed` branch in BookingListItem.tsx), and the API itself enforces nothing, so cancelled/past events can have attendees appended and calendar/email notifications sent out.

findings.title: Any attendee can add arbitrary guests to a booking, enabling email spam through the platform
findings.body: The permission check grants access to any existing attendee (`isAttendee`), and there is no limit on how many guests can be added or how often. Anyone who books a public event can then submit an arbitrary list of victim email addresses, and the handler will persist them as attendees and send them AttendeeScheduledEmail invitations containing the event details, organizer identity, and video meeting URL. This turns the endpoint into an unauthenticated-content email relay abusing Cal.com's sender reputation. The UI added in this PR only exposes the dialog on the organizer's bookings list, so the attendee permission appears broader than the feature requires; if attendee-added guests are intentional, they at least need rate limiting / a count cap.

findings.title: Duplicate detection and blacklist checks are case-sensitive
findings.body: Duplicate filtering uses `guest === attendee.email` and the blacklist uses `blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest)` where the blacklist entries are lowercased but `guest` is not. Email addresses differing only in case (e.g. `Alice@x.com` vs `alice@x.com`) are treated as distinct: the blacklist can be bypassed with mixed case, and `createMany` will insert a second Attendee row for an email that is already on the booking, producing duplicate attendees who then each receive emails. The dialog-side Set-based uniqueness check has the same flaw. Compare normalized (`toLowerCase()`/`trim()`) values on both sides.

findings.title: Guests added to seated (seatsPerTimeSlot) events get no BookingSeat reference
findings.body: For seated events, every attendee is expected to have a BookingSeat record (seat reference) — the handler even copies `seatsPerTimeSlot`/`seatsShowAttendees` onto the CalendarEvent, but it only creates plain Attendee rows via `createMany` and never creates BookingSeat entries. Guests added to a seated booking will have no `seatReferenceUid`, won't be counted against seat availability (so the slot can be overbooked), and any flows that rely on seat references (joining, cancelling a seat, rescheduling a seat) will break or behave inconsistently for them.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails ignores the event type's disableStandardEmails settings
findings.body: Every other sender in this file (sendScheduledEmails, sendLocationChangeEmails, sendCancelledEmails, etc.) accepts the event type metadata and skips host/attendee emails when `eventTypeDisableHostEmail`/`eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail` (metadata.disableStandardEmails) is set. `sendAddGuestsEmails` takes no `eventTypeMetadata` and unconditionally emails the organizer, all team members, and every attendee. Event types that explicitly disabled standard emails will still have emails sent whenever guests are added.

findings.title: sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the raw `guests` input instead of the deduplicated `uniqueGuests`
findings.body: The handler computes `uniqueGuests` (excluding emails already on the booking and blacklisted ones) but then calls `sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests)` with the original input. In `sendAddGuestsEmails`, any attendee whose email appears in that list is sent a full AttendeeScheduledEmail as if they were a brand-new guest — so an already-existing attendee who was (re-)submitted gets a fresh 'scheduled' confirmation email rather than the 'new guests added' notice. Pass `uniqueGuests` instead.

findings.title: Organizer email subject uses attendees[0].name, which may be an empty string
findings.body: The subject is built with `name: this.calEvent.attendees[0].name`. The handler creates the new guests with `name: ""` and includes them in `evt.attendees`; since the ordering of `attendees` after the booking update isn't guaranteed, `attendees[0]` can be one of the new nameless guests, producing a subject like 'Guests Added: 30 min meeting with  at ...'. The scheduled-email flow this copies assumes attendees[0] is the booker with a real name.
